title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: ANDRE'S BIG SWITCH
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight: Andre Wallace, from Spokane, Washington.
For eleven years, he answered phones and said sorry eighty times a day.
At night, he watched wiring videos. Hundreds of them.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: ALL TALK
segments.quote: Knowing is not enough; we must apply. Willing is not enough; we must do.
segments.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
lines: His mom asked why he'd never touched an actual wire.
Andre shrugged. I'm thirty-four, Mom. Too old.
She tapped her fridge magnet, from the German writer Goethe:
Knowing is not enough; we must apply. Willing is not enough; we must do.
That night, Andre applied to be an electrician's apprentice.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: POPS
segments.quote: If you want to improve, be content to be thought foolish and stupid.
segments.author: Epictetus
lines: He got in. The other apprentices were nineteen. They called him Pops.
His boss Rosa had a line from the Greek thinker Epictetus taped up:
If you want to improve, be content to be thought foolish and stupid.
So Andre asked every question. Especially the dumb ones.
By spring, the kids asked him.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: CRAWL SPACE
segments.quote: I've learned from experience that the greater part of our happiness or misery depends on our dispositions and not on our circumstances.
segments.author: Martha Washington
lines: The pay was half his old paycheck. Lots of peanut butter.
One January, under a house at eight degrees, he started grumbling.
Rosa quoted Martha Washington:
I've learned from experience that the greater part of our happiness or misery depends on our dispositions and not on our circumstances.
So he started humming instead. Badly. Rosa begged him to stop.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THREE POINTS
segments.quote: There will come a time when you believe everything is finished. That will be the beginning.
segments.author: Louis L'Amour
lines: Four years later, he failed the license exam by three points.
He sat in the parking lot, sure it was over.
His mom texted a line from Louis L'Amour, the cowboy novelist:
There will come a time when you believe everything is finished. That will be the beginning.
He studied two months and passed. He cried in that same parking lot, happier.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE ICE STORM
segments.quote: Nothing is too wonderful to be true, if it be consistent with the laws of nature.
segments.author: Michael Faraday
lines: Then an ice storm knocked out power at the senior center.
Andre found the bad connection in ten minutes. Lights on.
Old Mr. Pruitt called it magic. Andre quoted the scientist Michael Faraday:
Nothing is too wonderful to be true, if it be consistent with the laws of nature.
Not magic. Four years of homework.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE WHITE VAN
segments.quote: Blessed is he who has found his work; let him ask no other blessedness.
segments.author: Thomas Carlyle
lines: Today, Andre's white van says Wallace Electric.
His old call center hired him last month. He didn't apologize once.
Rosa mailed him a card from the Scottish writer Thomas Carlyle:
Blessed is he who has found his work; let him ask no other blessedness.
He framed it, next to his mom's fridge magnet.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start doing. Ask. Mind your mood. Begin again. Trust the work. Find your work.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start doing. Ask. Mind your mood. Begin again. Trust the work. Find your work.
I once changed a light bulb myself. The fire department was very kind.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
